# Breasts too fatty to measure

```{python}
#| include: false
from cohort_common import *
```

The rule of @sec-the-rule compares a patient only if both breasts have a usable scan. A breast with no usable scan is not
mismeasured; it is left out because every spot the beam hit was fat. Many of these breasts are genuinely NORMAL, and being too fatty to measure
is itself a result: that breast has little water. This section looks at those breasts, and at what happens if the test counts them as the
fattier breast instead of leaving the patient out.

```{python}
#| include: false
# each breast: its labels, usable scans and all scans
breast_info = defaultdict(lambda: [set(), 0, 0])
breast_scans = defaultdict(list)  # (nova, side): [(curve, usable)]
for nova, side, label, curve, height, centre in scan_records:
    keep = usable(height, centre, WATER_MIN, CENTRE_MIN)
    info = breast_info[nova, side]
    info[0].add(label); info[1] += keep; info[2] += 1
    breast_scans[nova, side].append((curve, keep))

def label_of(nova, side):
    info = breast_info.get((nova, side))
    return next(iter(info[0])) if info and len(info[0]) == 1 else None

def pair_name(nova):
    """'CANCER vs NORMAL' etc. (first-named breast expected to have more water), 'NORMAL vs NORMAL', or None."""
    labels = sorted((label_of(nova, "LEFT"), label_of(nova, "RIGHT")), key=str)
    if None in labels:
        return None
    if labels == ["NORMAL", "NORMAL"]:
        return "NORMAL vs NORMAL"
    for comparison, (base, others) in COMPARISONS.items():
        if base in labels and set(labels) - {base} <= set(others) and labels.count(base) == 1:
            return comparison
    return None

PAIR_NAMES = list(COMPARISONS) + ["NORMAL vs NORMAL"]
pair_of = {nova: pair_name(nova) for nova in analysis_novas}

# how many of each label's breasts have no usable scan
no_usable = {label: [breast_info[k][1] == 0 for k in breast_info if label_of(*k) == label] for label in COHORTS}
no_usable_table = "\n".join(["| Label | Breasts | No usable scan |", "|---|---|---|"]
                            + [f"| {label} | {len(flags)} | {sum(flags)} ({np.mean(flags):.0%}) |" for label, flags in no_usable.items()])

# each kind of patient: both breasts usable, one, or neither
def usable_sides(nova):
    return sum(breast_info[nova, side][1] > 0 for side in ("LEFT", "RIGHT"))

patients_table_rows = []
for name in PAIR_NAMES:
    novas = [n for n, p in pair_of.items() if p == name]
    counts = [sum(usable_sides(n) == k for n in novas) for k in (2, 1, 0)]
    patients_table_rows.append(f"| {name} | {len(novas)} | {counts[0]} | {counts[1]} | {counts[2]} ({counts[2] / len(novas):.0%}) |")
patients_table = "\n".join(["| Patients | All | Both breasts usable | One | Neither |", "|---|---|---|---|---|"] + patients_table_rows)

# the test with a breast that has no usable scan counted as the fattier one
use = rule_breasts(WATER_MIN, CENTRE_MIN)

def with_fatty(comparison):
    base, others = COMPARISONS[comparison]
    higher = compared = 0
    for nova, name in pair_of.items():
        if name != comparison:
            continue
        values = {}
        for side in ("LEFT", "RIGHT"):
            value = use[nova, side][1] if (nova, side) in use else -np.inf  # no usable scan: fattiest possible
            values[label_of(nova, side)] = value
        first, second = values[next(label for label in values if label != base)], values[base]
        if first == second or np.isnan(first) or np.isnan(second):
            continue  # both too fatty to measure: nothing to tell them apart
        compared += 1; higher += first > second
    return higher, compared, binomtest(higher, compared).pvalue if compared else np.nan

fixed = rule_results(WATER_MIN, CENTRE_MIN)
fatty = {c: with_fatty(c) for c in COMPARISONS}
result_table = "\n".join(["| Comparison | Both breasts usable | Counting a breast with no usable scan as the fattier |", "|---|---|---|"]
                         + [f"| {c} | {rule_text(fixed, c)}, p = {fixed[c][2]:.3f} | {rule_text(fatty, c)}, p = {fatty[c][2]:.3f} |"
                            for c in COMPARISONS])

nn_neither = [n for n, p in pair_of.items() if p == "NORMAL vs NORMAL" and usable_sides(n) == 0]
```

## Who has no usable scan

Breasts with no usable scan, by label:

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
print(no_usable_table)
```

And patients by how many of their breasts have a usable scan:

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
print(patients_table)
```

Of the `{python} sum(p == "NORMAL vs NORMAL" for p in pair_of.values())` patients with two NORMAL breasts,
`{python} len(nn_neither)` have no usable scan in either breast, so the rule never sees them (@fig-nn-fatty). These are the most typical healthy
patients in the study, and their breasts are fatty all the way through.

```{python}
#| label: fig-nn-fatty
#| fig-cap: "The NORMAL/NORMAL patients in which neither breast has a usable scan. Each panel is one patient: every prepared scan of the left (blue) and right (orange) breast, with the usable-scan water threshold over q 20–22 (black bar). The water peak never reaches the threshold."
SIDE_COLOURS = {"LEFT": "tab:blue", "RIGHT": "tab:orange"}
curves = [curve for n in nn_neither for side in ("LEFT", "RIGHT") for curve, _ in breast_scans[n, side]]
covered = np.flatnonzero(np.isfinite(np.vstack(curves)).all(axis=0))
columns = slice(covered[0], covered[-1] + 1)
y_top = 1.05 * np.nanmax(np.vstack(curves)[:, columns])

plt.rcParams["font.size"] = 7
n_cols = 4
n_rows = int(np.ceil(len(nn_neither) / n_cols))
fig, axes = plt.subplots(n_rows, n_cols, figsize=(8, 2.1 * n_rows), sharex=True, sharey=True, squeeze=False)
for ax, nova in zip(axes.flat, nn_neither):
    for side, colour in SIDE_COLOURS.items():
        for curve, _ in breast_scans[nova, side]:
            ax.plot(q[columns], curve[columns], color=colour, lw=0.9, alpha=0.8)
    ax.hlines(WATER_MIN, *WATER, color="black", lw=2)
    age = f", age {nova_age[nova]:.0f}" if nova in nova_age else ""
    ax.set_title(f"Nova {nova}{age}")
    ax.set(xlim=(2, q[columns][-1]), ylim=(0, y_top))
    ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
for ax in axes.flat[len(nn_neither):]:
    ax.axis("off")
for ax in axes[-1]:
    ax.set_xlabel("q (nm⁻¹)")
for ax in axes[:, 0]:
    ax.set_ylabel("I(q), stretched")
axes[0, 0].legend(handles=[Line2D([], [], color=c, label=s.lower()) for s, c in SIDE_COLOURS.items()], frameon=False, loc="upper right")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
plt.rcParams["font.size"] = 10
```

## Counting a fatty breast as a result

If a breast has no usable scan, the test can treat it as the fattier breast of the pair instead of dropping the patient. A patient whose
two breasts both have no usable scan is still left out: there is nothing to tell them apart.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
print(result_table)
```

For CANCER vs NORMAL this adds the patients where only the CANCER breast has a usable scan, which count as right, and those where only the
NORMAL breast has one, which count as wrong. The first kind outnumber the second, so more patients are compared with about the same strength
of evidence. For BENIGN vs NORMAL it goes the other way: more often it is the BENIGN breast that has no usable scan, and the result falls
further below chance. Most of the patients the rule drops are not lost wins, as in most of them both breasts are fatty.

Having two fatty breasts is much more common in NORMAL/NORMAL patients (`{python} f"{len(nn_neither) / sum(p == 'NORMAL vs NORMAL' for p in pair_of.values()):.0%}"`)
than in any other kind of patient (37–42%). So "too fatty to measure in both breasts" leans towards a healthy patient. NORMAL/NORMAL patients
are older, though (median age `{python} f"{np.median([nova_age[n] for n, p in pair_of.items() if p == 'NORMAL vs NORMAL' and n in nova_age]):.0f}"`
against `{python} f"{np.median([nova_age[n] for n, p in pair_of.items() if p and p != 'NORMAL vs NORMAL' and n in nova_age]):.0f}"` for the
other patients), and fatty breasts are common with age, so this may be age as much as health. With only
`{python} sum(p == "NORMAL vs NORMAL" for p in pair_of.values())` NORMAL/NORMAL patients it is a hint, not a result.
